title: Disbursements from the Rural Home Loans Escrow Account
content:
**Standard.** From the escrow account of a Rural Home Loans loan the association pays each property tax installment to the county treasurer before its delinquency date, each homeowner's and flood insurance premium to the insurer by its due date, and each month's mortgage insurance premium, as billed. A bill is paid even when the escrow balance is insufficient; the account then runs negative and the deficiency is recovered at the next analysis. Each tax year, policy term and mortgage insurance month is paid once. A loan with escrow waived has no disbursements, except flood insurance, which can never be waived for a dwelling in a special flood hazard area.

## Payment calendar

| Bill | Paid to | Paid by |
|---|---|---|
| Property tax installment | county treasurer | before its delinquency date |
| Homeowner's insurance premium | insurer | its due date |
| Flood insurance premium | insurer | its due date |
| Mortgage insurance premium | insurer | each month, as billed |

## One payment per bill

Before a disbursement is made, the escrow activity of the loan is read for a disbursement of the same kind for the same tax year, policy term or mortgage insurance month; each is paid once, whichever payee is named.

## Points of judgement

- *Hypothetical case:* escrow holds 600.00 USD when a property tax installment of 1450.00 USD falls due. The installment is paid in full; the balance becomes negative 850.00 and that deficiency is recovered at the next analysis.
- On a loan with escrow waived, no taxes or homeowner's premiums are paid from escrow; flood insurance on a dwelling in a special flood hazard area is still paid from escrow.
